title: Console admin workflows → audit events mapping (working doc)
content:
Context
- This is a working inventory of Console “admin workflows” that must emit audit events with canonical schema v1.
- Primary goal: ensure Console UI + Console backend actions are fully covered for sensitive actions, with consistent actor attribution and target semantics across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- This doc is NOT the schema itself; it maps user-visible workflows to event_type(s), the backend touchpoints, and validation notes.

Owners / touchpoints
- Console UI: Felix S. (w/ Dylan B.)
- Console backend (admin APIs): Chloe M.
- Schema/taxonomy validation: Marcus L. / Hanae S.
- Exporter/SIEM normalization: Kevin O.
- Coverage dashboard: Logan W.

Assumptions (aligning on semantics)
1) Console UI should NOT emit audit events directly.
   - UI triggers backend admin API calls; backend emits events (single source of truth).
   - Exception: “client-side only” actions are not sensitive (e.g., changing table columns) and should not be audited.

2) “Actor” attribution rules
   - actor.type: user | service_account | system
   - actor.id: Redwood principal id (NOT an email as primary identifier)
   - actor.impersonated_by.* present if Support/Solutions/SRE uses impersonation features (if/when enabled)
   - source.ip should be captured at gateway or backend edge; ensure forwarded-for normalization.

3) Correlation fields
   - Always include request_id and trace_id.
   - For multi-step Console workflows, include admin_action_id (stable across the workflow) so investigators can join multiple events.

4) Redaction rules
   - Never log secret material: API keys, client secrets, bearer tokens, SAML cert private keys, webhook secrets.
   - For keys: include key_id, name/label (if non-sensitive), and last4/preview ONLY if explicitly allowed by redaction spec.

5) When to emit events
   - Emit on “state change” (create/update/delete/rotate/enable/disable/apply).
   - Also emit on “security-relevant access” where required (e.g., viewing certain secret-bearing settings) — still under debate; see Open Questions.


Field checklist (what backend must provide at minimum)
(See Confluence “Audit event schema v1” for exact naming; checklist here is a practical reminder for implementers.)
- schema_version
- event_id (ULID preferred for time sorting; must be globally unique)
- event_time (RFC3339)
- event_type (must match registry)
- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private
- tenant_id, project_id (where applicable), environment (prod/staging where applicable)
- actor: type + id (+ auth_method if available)
- source: ip + user_agent (truncated / normalized)
- action: result (success|failure) + error_code (if failure)
- target/resource: resource_type + resource_id (+ display_name if low-cardinality)
- change_summary: before/after (must be constrained; see cardinality budget)


WORKFLOW MAP (UI → backend endpoint → audit event)
Format:
- Workflow name
- UI surface (route/component)
- Backend touchpoints (service + endpoint)
- Audit event_type(s)
- Notes / required fields / gotchas


A) RBAC / Access Management

A1) Create role
- UI: /settings/access/roles → “Create role” modal
- BE: console-backend → POST /admin/rbac/roles
- event_type: rbac.role.create
- Notes:
  - target.resource_type=rbac_role, target.resource_id=role_id
  - change_summary: include role_name + permission_set_id or permissions_count; avoid listing every permission string if high-cardinality.

A2) Update role (permissions/name)
- UI: /settings/access/roles/{roleId} → edit + save
- BE: PUT /admin/rbac/roles/{roleId}
- event_type: rbac.role.update
- Notes:
  - include diff summary: fields_changed=[name, permissions] and permissions_added_count/removed_count
  - ensure “no-op save” does not emit (or emits with outcome=no_change) — decide and be consistent.

A3) Delete role
- UI: /settings/access/roles/{roleId} → “Delete role”
- BE: DELETE /admin/rbac/roles/{roleId}
- event_type: rbac.role.delete
- Notes:
  - Include whether role was in-use; if deletion blocked, emit failure with error_code=ROLE_IN_USE.

A4) Assign role to user / service account
- UI: /settings/access/members → change role dropdown
- BE: POST /admin/rbac/assignments (or PUT /admin/rbac/members/{memberId}/role)
- event_type: rbac.assignment.create (or rbac.assignment.update if existing)
- Notes:
  - target is the member principal being granted access: target.resource_type=principal, target.resource_id=principal_id
  - include assigned_role_id in change_summary

A5) Remove member / revoke access
- UI: /settings/access/members → “Remove”
- BE: DELETE /admin/rbac/members/{memberId}
- event_type: rbac.membership.delete
- Notes:
  - include member_type (user/service_account) as enum

A6) Break-glass / admin elevation (if exposed in Console)
- UI: /settings/access/break-glass
- BE: POST /admin/rbac/break_glass/enable; POST /admin/rbac/break_glass/disable
- event_type: rbac.break_glass.enable, rbac.break_glass.disable
- Notes:
  - High sensitivity: must include approver context if any (approved_by principal id)
  - Ensure Private parity (operator identity may be different).


B) API Keys / Credentials

B1) Create API key (user or service account)
- UI: /settings/api-keys → “Create key”
- BE: POST /admin/credentials/api_keys
- event_type: credential.api_key.create
- Notes:
  - DO NOT log key material.
  - target.resource_type=api_key, target.resource_id=key_id
  - change_summary: key_name/label (if allowed), scopes_count, expiration_set=true/false

B2) Rotate API key
- UI: /settings/api-keys/{keyId} → “Rotate key”
- BE: POST /admin/credentials/api_keys/{keyId}:rotate
- event_type: credential.api_key.rotate
- Notes:
  - include rotated_from_key_id (or previous_key_version) only if schema supports; otherwise store in change_summary as a stable id.

B3) Revoke API key
- UI: /settings/api-keys/{keyId} → “Revoke”
- BE: POST /admin/credentials/api_keys/{keyId}:revoke (or DELETE)
- event_type: credential.api_key.revoke
- Notes:
  - change_summary: revoke_reason enum (user_initiated, suspected_compromise, policy_change)

B4) Update API key metadata (name, expiration)
- UI: /settings/api-keys/{keyId} → edit
- BE: PUT /admin/credentials/api_keys/{keyId}
- event_type: credential.api_key.update
- Notes:
  - ensure only metadata changes; if scope changes exist, treat as separate event_type (open question).


C) Audit log export configuration (customer SIEM)

C1) Create export destination (Splunk HEC)
- UI: /settings/audit-logs/export → “Add destination” → Splunk
- BE: POST /admin/audit_log_exports
- event_type: audit.export_destination.create
- Notes:
  - target.resource_type=audit_export_destination, target.resource_id=destination_id
  - change_summary should include destination_type=splunk_hec, endpoint_host (NOT full URL path if it includes sensitive tokens), tls_enabled boolean
  - credentials: DO NOT log HEC token; if validation fails, emit failure with error_code=INVALID_AUTH.

C2) Create export destination (Azure Sentinel)
- UI: /settings/audit-logs/export → “Add destination” → Sentinel
- BE: POST /admin/audit_log_exports
- event_type: audit.export_destination.create
- Notes:
  - change_summary: destination_type=azure_sentinel, workspace_id (ok), dcr_id (ok)
  - do not log shared_key / client_secret.

C3) Update export destination (endpoint, batching, filters)
- UI: /settings/audit-logs/export/{destId} → edit
- BE: PUT /admin/audit_log_exports/{destId}
- event_type: audit.export_destination.update
- Notes:
  - include fields_changed list + before/after for small booleans/ints; avoid logging free-form filter strings if unbounded.

C4) Delete export destination
- UI: /settings/audit-logs/export/{destId} → delete
- BE: DELETE /admin/audit_log_exports/{destId}
- event_type: audit.export_destination.delete

C5) Enable/disable export destination
- UI: /settings/audit-logs/export/{destId} → toggle
- BE: POST /admin/audit_log_exports/{destId}:enable, :disable
- event_type: audit.export_destination.enable, audit.export_destination.disable

C6) Test export destination (send synthetic event)
- UI: /settings/audit-logs/export/{destId} → “Send test”
- BE: POST /admin/audit_log_exports/{destId}:test
- event_type: audit.export_destination.test
- Notes:
  - Must be audited (it is an action against security telemetry).
  - Do not embed the synthetic event payload in the audit event.


D) Retention / Data residency settings (Console-controlled)

D1) Update audit log retention period
- UI: /settings/audit-logs/retention → save
- BE: PUT /admin/audit_logging/retention
- event_type: audit.retention.update
- Notes:
  - include old_retention_days, new_retention_days
  - clarify scope: tenant vs project (include scope enum)

D2) Update data residency region for audit logs (if configurable)
- UI: /settings/audit-logs/residency → select region
- BE: PUT /admin/audit_logging/residency
- event_type: audit.data_residency.update
- Notes:
  - include old_region, new_region (enum)


E) Policy / Routing changes exposed via Console (rollouts + fallbacks)
(These are sometimes in “Console & Rollouts”; including here for completeness since the action occurs in Console.)

E1) Update routing policy (fallbacks/allow-lists)
- UI: /settings/routing/policies/{policyId} → edit and apply
- BE: policy-service via console-backend → PUT /admin/policies/{policyId}
- event_type: policy.routing.update
- Notes:
  - include policy_id, policy_version
  - diff generation must be cardinality-safe (e.g., counts + stable ids; avoid dumping large JSON policy).

E2) Enable/disable model for tenant/project
- UI: /settings/models → toggle model availability
- BE: PUT /admin/models/{modelId}/availability
- event_type: model.availability.update
- Notes:
  - include model_id, old_state, new_state


F) Org/Tenant security settings (Console)

F1) IP allow-list update
- UI: /settings/security/ip-allowlist
- BE: PUT /admin/security/ip_allowlist
- event_type: security.ip_allowlist.update
- Notes:
  - Danger of high-cardinality: do not log full list if large. Prefer counts + hash of normalized set, and optionally log only delta (added/removed CIDRs) capped to N entries.

F2) SSO (SAML/OIDC) configuration update
- UI: /settings/security/sso
- BE: PUT /admin/security/sso
- event_type: security.sso.update
- Notes:
  - Do not log x509 cert private data, client_secret, or raw SAML metadata.
  - include provider_type enum + enabled true/false.

F3) SCIM provisioning enable/disable (if present)
- UI: /settings/security/scim
- BE: POST /admin/security/scim:enable / :disable
- event_type: security.scim.enable, security.scim.disable
- Notes:
  - SCIM token must never be logged.


UI/BE instrumentation notes (Console backend)
- All admin endpoints should pass through an “audit middleware” that:
  - constructs actor and correlation from auth context
  - sets source.ip from trusted headers (use gateway-provided normalized header)
  - enforces event_type registration (build-time + runtime guard)
  - attaches outcome=success|failure
- For multi-object operations (e.g., bulk member import), emit:
  - one summary event (preferred) OR
  - per-target events only if volume is capped and event size controlled.


Validation / test checklist (what we need for “done”)
- For each workflow above:
  - Integration test executes the action and asserts a v1-shaped event exists with correct event_type and required fields.
  - Negative test: failure path still emits an event with outcome=failure and safe error_code.
  - Verify no secrets appear in emitted payload (lint + runtime sample).
- Coverage dashboard should show:
  - expected_event_types (from registry) vs observed in last 24h, broken down by service=console-backend.


Known gaps (as of last pass 2026-02-24)
- Role update diff is currently too verbose in staging (contains full permission list). Needs summarization.
- Export destination “test” endpoint emits event but missing admin_action_id.
- IP allow-list update: cardinality budget not finalized; need final approach (delta vs hash).


Open questions (need decisions; please comment in doc / Slack thread)
1) Do we audit “view” actions in Console for sensitive pages?
   - Example: viewing export destination settings where endpoint host is shown.
   - Current leaning: do not audit reads unless they expose secrets; but we should ensure secrets are never shown after initial creation anyway.

2) For bulk operations (member import / RBAC batch changes), do we emit one summary event or N per-member events?
   - SIEM customers prefer per-target sometimes, but event volume may explode.

3) Should rbac.assignment.update be separate from create/delete?
   - Implementation preference: create/update/delete are distinct; taxonomy currently ambiguous in some services.

4) Should we include actor_email?
   - If included, should it be hashed or omitted for PII minimization? (GRC wants traceability; Security wants minimization.)


Notes to self (Chloe)
- Sync with Kevin on exporter normalization expectations for console-backend events.
- Ask Logan if coverage dashboard can ingest “expected workflows” list or only event_type list.
- Confirm with Olga what evidence screenshots they want from Console vs queries from SIEM.
